newsitem.title: BULGARIA: PRESS DIGEST - BULGARIAN BUSINESS WEEKLIES -AUG 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - BULGARIAN BUSINESS WEEKLIES -AUG 18.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Bulgarian business weeklies on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:

-- Rem Vyakhirev, chairman of the Russian gas monopoly Gazprom, said in an interview with the Bulgarian National Television he agreed to a proposal by Bulgaria's government to restore the 50/50 percent state participation of Bulgaria and Russia in the gas joint stock company Topenergy.

Last month Bulgaria's cabinet asked Bulgarian private firms in Topenergy to transfer their stakes to the state-owned Bulgargas company in a bid to restore its original 50 percent participation in the joint venture.

-- Potential buyers of Bulgarian firms offered for privatisation would be required to prove the origin of their money to local tax authorities under a draft decree tentatively approved by the government last week.

-- Bulgaria's industry ministry sealed seven privatisation deals for stakes in industrial firms worth a total of 1.347 billion levs. Buyers also pledged to invest additional $1.02 million in the firms.
-- Bulgaria's central bank said it would tighten controls on the operations of the country's financial brokerages to ensure compliance with new central bank regulations.

-- Bulgaria's private Balkan Universal Bank shareholders decided to adopt a two-tier management system for the bank and to raise capital to 2.3 billion levs from 800 million levs to meet new, higher minimum capital requirements.
-- Bulgarian commercial banks should raise their capital to 10 billion levs by end-June 1998 to meet new central bank minimum capital requirements. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-981-41-45
